title: Internal probe led to graft case vs employees – Landbank
summary: The Land Bank of the Philippines (LBP) said its internal investigation prompted the filing of a graft complaint against three long-sacked employees and a businessman over alleged irregularities…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Land Bank of the Philippines (LBP) said its internal investigation prompted the filing of a graft complaint against three long-sacked employees and a businessman over alleged irregularities involving a P115-million loan.

In a statement, the state-run firm said it filed the complaint before the Office of the Ombudsman on May 26, 2022 after uncovering alleged irregularities in a loan transaction granted to American Boulevard Trading Corp. (ABTC).
“The ombudsman’s decision to pursue graft charges is a result of the complaint filed by Landbank and validates the bank’s actions in bringing the matter before the proper authorities,” it said.

The ombudsman previously announced that it found prima facie evidence with reasonable certainty of conviction against former LBP first vice president Lolita Silva, former assistant vice president Danilo Dayanghirang, former account officer Ronaldo Robles and ABTC president and chairman Alberto Ching for violation of the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act.
Landbank said the transaction was processed by the three former employees, identified as Silva, Dayanghirang and Robles, who had already left the state-run lender in January and March 2020.
Silva’s employment ended on Jan. 31, 2020, while Dayanghirang and Robles left the bank on March 3, 2020 and Jan. 17, 2020, respectively.
The bank said it maintains zero tolerance for misconduct and would take appropriate action against officials or employees found accountable.
Landbank net income had risen by eight percent to P37.53 billion as of end-September from P34.86 billion last year.
